questions.question: Examine the following Command Output Which two conclusions can you make from the output of the tracert command? (Choose 2.)
options: The trace successfully reached the www.cisco.com server.
The trace failed after the fourth hop.
The IPv6 address associated with the www.cisco.com server is 2600:1408: c400: 38d: : b33.
The routers at hops 5 and 6 are offline.
The device sending the trace has IPv6 address 2600:1408:c400:38d :: b33.
answers: The trace successfully reached the www.cisco.com server.
The IPv6 address associated with the www.cisco.com server is 2600:1408: c400: 38d: : b33.
questions.explanation:
✅ Correct pair: the trace reached www.cisco.com, and the IPv6 address 2600:1408:c400:38d::b33 belongs to the Cisco server.
• In tracert output the LAST line is the destination. Hop 12 shows the final address, so the trace completed successfully.
• The address listed at the destination hop is the address of the server being traced (not of your own PC).

❌ "Trace failed after the fourth hop" and "routers at hops 5 and 6 are offline" → hops 5–6 only show "Request timed out" (* * *). Many routers ignore or filter ICMP, but traffic still passes through them, and the later hops answer, proving the path works.
❌ "The sending device has IPv6 address 2600:…::b33" → that is the destination's address, not the sender's.

💡 How to read tracert: stars in the MIDDLE = that router doesn't answer, normal. Stars at the END (the trace never reaches the target) = the problem is at or after the last responding hop. The trace reaches its destination at hop 12. The timeouts at hops 5 and 6 only show that those hops did not answer; intermediate routers often filter or deprioritize traceroute probes.

questions.question: Which two pieces of information should you include when you initially create a support ticket? (Choose 2.)
options: A detailed description of the fault
Details about the computers connected to the network
A description of the conditions when the fault occurs
The actions taken to resolve the fault
The description of the top-down fault-finding procedure
answers: A detailed description of the fault
A description of the conditions when the fault occurs
questions.explanation:
✅ When you first open a support ticket, write: (1) a detailed description of the fault and (2) the conditions when the fault occurs (when it started, what you were doing, how often, who is affected). This gives the next technician a clear picture.

❌ Details about computers on the network → too broad; it can be added later if needed.
❌ Actions taken to resolve the fault → added later as you work (the ticket's history log).
❌ Description of top-down fault-finding → a method, not information from the user.

💡 Initial ticket = WHAT is wrong + WHEN/under what conditions.

questions.question: Which two statements are true about the IPv4 address of the default gateway configured on a host? (Choose 2.)
options: The IPv4 address of the default gateway must be the first host address in the subnet.
The same default gateway IPv4 address is configured on each host on the local network.
The default gateway is the Loopback0 interface IPv4 address of the router connected to the same local network as the host.
The default gateway is the IPv4 address of the router interface connected to the same local network as the host.
Hosts learn the default gateway IPv4 address through router advertisement messages.
answers: The same default gateway IPv4 address is configured on each host on the local network.
The default gateway is the IPv4 address of the router interface connected to the same local network as the host.
questions.explanation:
✅ Correct pair: "The same default gateway address is configured on each host of the local network" and "The default gateway is the IPv4 address of the router interface connected to the same local network as the host".
• The default gateway is your "door to other networks". Every host on the same LAN uses the SAME door, and that door is the router interface (or Layer 3 switch interface) that sits on THAT LAN.

❌ "Must be the first host address in the subnet" → common habit (.1) but not a rule. Any valid, unused host address of the subnet can be used.
❌ "Is the Loopback0 interface address of the router" → a loopback is a virtual interface inside the router. Hosts cannot reach it as a door. The gateway must be the connected (LAN-side) interface.
❌ "Hosts learn the gateway through router advertisement messages" → RA messages belong to IPv6. IPv4 hosts get the gateway from DHCP or from manual configuration.

💡 Without a default gateway a host can only talk to devices in its own subnet.

questions.question: An administrator is configuring the host PC-A on the network shown in the following graphic. PC-A must be able to communicate on the local network and on the internet. There is no DHCP server on the network. What information does the administrator need to input in the IPV4 protocol properties window? Match each item to its correct description.
answers: IP address → Unused host in 172.100.0.0/16, e.g. 172.100.0.10
questions.explanation:
The PC must be able to talk to the LAN AND the internet, with no DHCP, so you must type three settings by hand:

• IP address → an UNUSED address inside the same subnet as the router: 172.100.0.0/16 network. For example 172.100.0.10. Don't use .1 (the router) or .254 (the server already using it).
• Subnet mask → 255.255.0.0 (that's /16).
• Default gateway → 172.100.0.1, the router's interface on PC-A's own LAN (Router1 G0/0). Not the ISP side (10.10.100.x).

💡 Add a DNS server too if you want to open sites by name. Checklist: IP + Mask + Gateway (+ DNS).

1) Start with the question: Start with the host’s view: it needs a stable default gateway even when one router fails. A first-hop redundancy group supplies a virtual gateway, backed by multiple physical routers. The host uses the virtual IP and the associated virtual MAC.
2) Work through it: For HSRP, identify the active router that forwards and the elected standby that is ready to replace it. Higher priority is preferred; preemption allows an eligible higher-priority router to reclaim the active role. Default hello/hold timers are three and ten seconds unless configured otherwise.

questions.question: A help desk technician receives the four trouble tickets listed below. Which ticket should receive the highest priority and be addressed first?
options: Ticket 1: A user requests relocation of a printer to a different network jack in the same office. The jack must be patched and made active.
Ticket 2: An online webinar is taking place in the conference room. The video conferencing equipment lost internet access.
Ticket 3: A user reports that response time for a cloud-based application is slower than usual.
Ticket 4: Two users report that wireless access in the cafeteria has been down for the last hour.
answers: Ticket 2: An online webinar is taking place in the conference room. The video conferencing equipment lost internet access.
questions.explanation:
✅ Ticket 2 (the live webinar lost internet access). Priority = IMPACT (how many people/how important) + URGENCY (is it happening right now / time-sensitive).
A live event is happening now and a business-critical service is already down, so it comes first.

❌ Ticket 1 (printer relocation) → planned work, low urgency.
❌ Ticket 3 (cloud app slower) → degraded but working, medium.
❌ Ticket 4 (cafeteria Wi-Fi down for an hour) → affects several users and is worth fixing soon, but it isn't tied to a live critical event. It's the second-best candidate.

💡 Outage + live deadline > partial outage > slow performance > request/change.

questions.question: You are a senior network administrator tasked with diagnosing intermittent connectivity issues on the executive floor of a multinational corporation, which primarily uses iOS devices. After initial checks, you suspect that the problem may be related to SSID settings and network configuration specifics not aligning correctly with the corporate security protocols. Given the high-security requirements and the exclusive use of iOS devices on this floor, which approach should you take to verify and rectify the network settings directly on the affected devices?
questions.explanation:
✅ Manual Configuration: directly open the Wi-Fi settings of the iPhone/iPad (Settings → Wi-Fi → (i) next to the network) and check the SSID, the security type (WPA2/WPA3), the password and the IP settings (Automatic vs Manual) one device at a time, and correct them. That verifies the exact settings on each affected device.

❌ Network Reset → wipes ALL saved Wi-Fi, cellular and VPN settings: too destructive and it doesn't help you find which setting is wrong.
❌ Use Fing → a scanner app that discovers devices on a network. It doesn't check the iOS device's own Wi-Fi settings.
❌ SSID Reconfiguration → changing the network name on the access point, which does not verify the devices.

💡 Useful iOS steps: Forget This Network → rejoin; check the Private Wi-Fi Address option; check IP configuration.

questions.question: Which two statements are true about the impact to communication on the network while the router is temporarily offline. Evaluate the Graphic.
options: None of the PC’s can access the file server (File-Srv)
The file server (File-Srv) can still access the internet
PC-A and PC-B can still communicate with each other.
PC-A , PC-B, PC-C and PC-D can still communicate with each other
PC-C and PC-D can still communicate with the file server (File-Srv)
answers: None of the PC’s can access the file server (File-Srv)
PC-A and PC-B can still communicate with each other.
questions.explanation:
✅ Correct pair: A and C.
• Router1 is the ONLY path between different VLANs (VLAN 100, VLAN 110, VLAN 10). If it's offline, devices in different VLANs can't talk. The file server is in another VLAN than the PCs, so none of the PCs can reach it → statement A is true.
• PC-A and PC-B are in the SAME VLAN on the same switch, so they still communicate through the switch without a router → statement C is true.

❌ B: The file server can still reach the internet → false, the router is the path to the internet.
❌ D: PC-A, B, C and D can all still talk → false; A/B and C/D are in different VLANs (100 vs 110), and crossing VLANs needs the router.
❌ E: PC-C and PC-D can still reach File-Srv → false; File-Srv is in VLAN 10, different VLAN.

⚠ The slide highlighted A and D. D is wrong; the right pair is A and C.
💡 Same VLAN = switch is enough. Different VLAN or the internet = router needed. With Router1 offline, VLANs 100 and 110 cannot route to one another. PC-A and PC-B remain in the same local VLAN and subnet, so they can still communicate.

questions.question: Which action does Switch1 take?
options: Switch1 queries Switch2 for the MAC address of PC-C
Switch1 drops the frame and sends an error message back to PC-A
Switch1 sends an ARP request to obtain the MAC address of PC-C
Switch1 floods the frame out all active ports except port Gi0/1
answers: Switch1 floods the frame out all active ports except port Gi0/1
questions.explanation:
✅ Switch1 floods the frame out all active ports except port Gi0/1 (the port where it came in).
Why: The destination MAC address of PC-C is not in Switch1's MAC address table yet, so it is an UNKNOWN UNICAST. A switch's 3 rules are: (1) learn the source MAC and port, (2) forward to the known port if the destination is known, (3) if it is unknown or a broadcast → FLOOD to all ports except the incoming one. PC-C will reply, and the switch learns it.

❌ Query Switch2 for the MAC → switches don't ask each other.
❌ Drop the frame and send an error to PC-A → switches don't send errors for this.
❌ Send an ARP request → ARP is sent by hosts (and routers), not by a Layer 2 switch.

💡 The incoming port is never used for the flood (to avoid loops). The destination MAC is unknown, so the Layer 2 switch floods the frame in that VLAN out eligible ports except the incoming port Gi0/1.

questions.question: A laptop sends a broadcast into Switch 1 on port A. Switch 2 connects to port D on Switch 1. Which Switch 1 ports forward the broadcast?
questions.explanation:
✅ B, C and D only. Frame arrived on port A. A BROADCAST frame (or an unknown destination) is flooded out every port in the VLAN EXCEPT the one it came in on. So the other ports (B, C and D) send it out, while A does not.

❌ "D only" → forgets B and C. ❌ "A, B and D only" → includes A (the incoming port) and leaves out C. ❌ "B and C only" → forgets D.

💡 Broadcast = everyone in the broadcast domain (the VLAN) except the sender's port. Routers do NOT forward broadcasts, so they separate broadcast domains. The laptop sends a broadcast into Switch 1 on port A; Switch 2 is connected to port D. A switch forwards a broadcast out B, C, and D.

questions.question: A support technician examines the front panel of a Cisco switch and sees 4 Ethernet cables connected in the first four ports. Port 1,2 and 3 have a green LED. Port 4 has a blinking green light. What is the state of the Port 4?
options: Link is up and not stable
Link is up and there is no activity
Link is up with cable malfunctions
questions.explanation:
✅ Link is up and active. Port LED meanings on a Cisco switch:
• Off = no link (no cable, device off, or port shut down)
• Solid GREEN = link up, but no traffic right now (ports 1, 2, 3)
• BLINKING GREEN = link up and traffic passing = ACTIVE (port 4)
• Alternating green/amber = link fault (many errors)
• Amber = port not forwarding (for example blocked by STP)

So ports 1–3 are connected but idle, and port 4 is connected and transferring data.

💡 Traffic light: green = go · blinking = busy · amber = careful/problem.

questions.question: A user reports a problem connecting to network resources. Other users connected to the same switch are not experiencing the same problem. The user's computer is patched to a switch port Gi0/15. The status indicator for this port is blinking alternately green then amber. What does the light pattern indicate about the status of port Gi0/15?
options: The port is experiencing a high rate of errors.
The port is blocked by a firewall rule.
The port is not connected to a powered -on device.
answers: The port is experiencing a high rate of errors.
questions.explanation:
✅ A port LED that alternates green and amber means the link has a FAULT: a high rate of errors (bad cable, bad connector, duplex mismatch, interference). The user has a problem and others on the same switch don't → the fault is on that single port/cable. Replace/re-seat the patch cable, check the duplex/speed, check the NIC.

❌ Administratively shut down → the LED is off. ❌ Blocked by a firewall rule → firewalls are not switch port LEDs, and a switch LED doesn't show that. ❌ Not connected to a powered-on device → LED off (no link).

💡 Tip: use show interfaces gi0/15 to see CRC/input errors and duplex.

questions.question: What can you tell from the command output? A user report that a company website is not available. The help desk technician issues a tracert command to determine if the server hosting the website is reachable over the network. The output of the command is shown as follows:
options: The server with address 192.168.1.10 is reachable over the network
The router at hop 3 is not forwarding packets to the IP address 192.168.1.10
Requests to the web server at 192.168.1.10 are being delayed and time out.
The server address 192.168.1.10 is being blocked by a firewall on the router at hop3.
answers: The server with address 192.168.1.10 is reachable over the network
questions.explanation:
✅ The server 192.168.1.10 is reachable. Look at the LAST line (the destination) of the tracert: hop 5 shows 192.168.1.10 and it answered. Hop 3 only shows "Request timed out" (* * *): that router just doesn't reply to ICMP, but it still forwards traffic, as proven by the replies from the hops after it.

❌ "The router at hop 3 is not forwarding packets" → if it didn't, the later hops wouldn't answer.
❌ "Requests are delayed and time out" → the final hop replied.
❌ "The server is blocked by a firewall on the router at hop 3" → same reason: later hops answer.

💡 If the website is still unavailable, the problem is likely at the application/web service (port 80/443, server software) rather than the network path. The final traceroute hop is 192.168.1.10, so the destination is reachable. A timeout at one intermediate hop does not mean later traffic failed.

questions.question: At the Cisco router prompt router1#, which action is available in privileged EXEC mode?
options: Run show commands such as show running-config
Enter interface subcommands without selecting an interface
Change an interface address without entering configuration mode
answers: Run show commands such as show running-config
questions.explanation:
✅ Show running system information. The prompt ends with "#" (router1#), which means PRIVILEGED EXEC mode. In this mode you can run show commands (show running-config, show version, etc.).

❌ Enable a routing process, select an interface to configure, enter interface IP subcommands → all require GLOBAL CONFIGURATION mode (configure terminal) or interface configuration mode.

Modes: Router> = user EXEC (limited) → enable → Router# = privileged EXEC → configure terminal → Router(config)# → interface g0/1 → Router(config-if)#.

⚠ Your note says "1. User exec" for router1#: that's not right. router1> would be user EXEC; router1# is privileged EXEC. The router1# prompt is privileged EXEC mode. It can run show commands; enter global or interface configuration mode to change settings.

questions.question: What can you determine about this switch from the command output? Examine the output of the show mac-address-table command on a Cisco 24 ports Ethernet switch
options: There are eleven active ports on this switch
Port Fa0/5 is set to administratively down.
All entries were learned by examining incoming frames.
Port Gi0/1 connects to another switch
answers: Port Gi0/1 connects to another switch
questions.explanation:
✅ Port Gi0/1 connects to another switch. Look at the MAC address table: when ONE port shows MANY different MAC addresses (and several VLANs), those devices live behind another switch (an uplink/trunk).

❌ "Eleven active ports" → eleven is the number of ENTRIES (MAC addresses), not ports; the output shows only a few ports.
❌ "Fa0/5 is administratively down" → Fa0/5 has a STATIC entry in the table, which is a manually typed MAC, not a shutdown port.
❌ "All entries learned by examining incoming frames" → no, a STATIC entry is configured by an administrator, not learned.

💡 Type column: DYNAMIC = learned from traffic (ages out) · STATIC = typed in by an admin. Gi0/1 has dynamically learned MAC addresses from multiple VLANs, which is consistent with a switch trunk/uplink.

questions.question: For each statement, choose True or False.
statements: A device connected to GigabitEthernet0/1 can send out broadcast traffic.
A technician issued the shutdown command on interface GigabitEthernet0/2.
A technician set the IP address for GigabitEthernet0/0 by using the CLI.
statementNotes: The exhibit shows GigabitEthernet0/1 as down/down, so it cannot forward frames.
The interface status is administratively down, indicating it was disabled in configuration.
The Method column shows manual for GigabitEthernet0/0, indicating a manually configured address.
questions.explanation:
1. False — The exhibit shows GigabitEthernet0/1 as down/down, so it cannot forward frames.
2. True — The interface status is administratively down, indicating it was disabled in configuration.
3. True — The Method column shows manual for GigabitEthernet0/0, indicating a manually configured address.

questions.question: A new switch’s running configuration lists interface GigabitEthernet0/1 and 0/2 with no other settings. What can you conclude from the shown lines?
options: Both ports have manually assigned IP addresses.
The shown configuration does not indicate shutdown or assigned IP addresses.
The switch has no Layer 2 ports.
answers: The shown configuration does not indicate shutdown or assigned IP addresses.
questions.explanation:
A brand-new switch, connected through the console, and the output of a show command:

• "The two interfaces can communicate over Layer 2" → TRUE. Switch ports are enabled by default and work at Layer 2 (frames/MACs).
• "The two interfaces are administratively shut down" → FALSE. There is no "shutdown" line in their configuration. On a switch, ports are on by default (on a ROUTER the interfaces are shut down by default).
• "The two interfaces have a default IP address assigned" → FALSE. Switch ports are Layer 2 ports and have no IP address by default.

💡 A port with no "shutdown" line is enabled. Use show run | section interface to filter that part of the configuration. The shown running configuration only identifies two interface sections. Nothing shown assigns IP addresses or shuts the ports down; default switchports belong to VLAN 1.

In the ipconfig /all output, the DNS server address is 64.100.8.8 (not the DHCP server 192.168.10.1). tracert lists every router between the PC and that server.

💡 In ipconfig /all, don't mix up: DHCP Server (gives IP settings) vs DNS Servers (resolve names). (The slide has no marked answer.) The ipconfig output lists the DNS server as 64.100.8.8. Tracert to that address displays the path to the resolver.

questions.question: A web application uses https://www.companypro.net:7100/api. Which Wireshark display filter selects TCP packets using that port?

Two kinds of filters in Wireshark:
• Capture filter (set BEFORE capturing, BPF syntax): host www.companypro.net and tcp port 7100.
• Display filter (typed in the top bar AFTER capturing): ip.addr == 10.0.0.5 · tcp.port == 7100 · dns · icmp.

💡 First find the server IP with nslookup if needed. (The slide has no marked answer.) The URL specifies TCP port 7100. tcp.port == 7100 is a Wireshark display filter for packets using that port.

questions.question: In a network with multiple VLANs, a user is unable to communicate with other users in the same VLAN but can communicate with users in different VLANs. Which of the following could be the cause of this issue?

user's switchport is not assigned to the correct VLAN.

questions.question: In DHCP’s DORA exchange, what does a client send first when requesting a lease?

The client broadcasts Discover; a server may then Offer, the client Requests, and the server Acknowledges.

questions.question: Which WAN topology is most appropriate for a centrally located server farm with several satellite branches?

1) Start with the question: Separate access technology from service characteristics. Satellite internet reaches users through space-based radio links, while municipal Wi-Fi and WiMAX describe other forms of wireless access. They are examples of broadband wireless rather than one interchangeable protocol.
2) Work through it: Consider the deployment need: a rural location may use satellite when terrestrial broadband is unavailable. Coverage, latency, capacity and installation constraints must be considered independently instead of judging a service only by a single speed figure.
3) Apply the distinction: Distinguish a legacy textbook comparison from a specification. Upload-to-download ratios and comparisons with analog modems describe particular historical services; they are not universal numbers for every modern satellite system.

questions.question: What is a wireless security mode that requires a RADIUS server to authenticate wireless users?
questions.explanation:
✅ Enterprise wireless authentication uses an AAA server, commonly RADIUS, to validate individual user credentials. Personal wireless security instead uses a shared passphrase.
💡 Enterprise = individual identities + authentication server.

1) Start with the question: Determine whether the question asks about identity, permission or an activity record. Authentication checks who the user is; authorization decides which requested actions are allowed; accounting records use and activity. They solve different parts of access control.
2) Work through it: Map the wording: usernames/passwords point to authentication, allowed commands/resources point to authorization, and logs or usage reports point to accounting. Local AAA keeps credential information on the device; server-based AAA centralizes it through a service such as RADIUS or TACACS+.
3) Apply the distinction: For 802.1X, name the three roles: the supplicant requests access, the switch or AP acts as authenticator, and the authentication server validates the request. Enterprise Wi-Fi commonly uses this arrangement so each user has an individual identity.
❌ Common mix-ups: Do not treat SSH, HTTPS, RADIUS and SNMP as interchangeable. SSH/HTTPS protect management sessions, RADIUS supports AAA exchanges, and SNMP is used for monitoring/management. A source key that assigns the wrong job to one of these protocols needs a warning, not an invented justification.

questions.question: Which device allows users to connect to the network using a single or double radio?

💡 AP connects clients; WLC coordinates APs.

1) Start with the question: Identify whether the question concerns an AP, a controller, or discovery by a client. An AP provides wireless access to the LAN. A WLC centrally manages controller-based APs; an autonomous AP is configured independently.

LWAPP is older terminology found in the course material. Controller screens and available interface options depend on the software version.
3) Apply the distinction: For discovery, a beacon advertises a WLAN, while a client probe request actively searches. A non-advertised SSID may require a client to name it explicitly. An SSID identifies a network; the administrator password protects management and the wireless credentials protect admission.
❌ Common mix-ups: Hiding an SSID is not encryption or strong access control. Bluetooth support is model-dependent rather than the definition of an AP. A controller is not just a replacement name for an AP, and choosing the correct SSID is different from validating credentials.

questions.question: Which one is a technique for mitigating VLAN attacks?
options: Set the native VLAN to an unused VLAN.
answers: Set the native VLAN to an unused VLAN.
questions.explanation:
✅ Automatic trunk negotiation can let an attacker establish a trunk. Configure access ports explicitly, configure real trunks manually, disable unnecessary DTP negotiation, and keep the native VLAN unused by clients.
💡 Access ports stay access; trunks are deliberate.

3) Apply the distinction: For double tagging, follow the frame: the first switch can remove an outer tag associated with its native VLAN, exposing a second tag for another VLAN. Separating users from the native VLAN reduces this opportunity; permitted VLAN lists further limit trunk scope.
❌ Common mix-ups: BPDU guard addresses unexpected spanning-tree participation, not every VLAN-hopping mechanism. DHCP snooping, DAI and IP Source Guard address different trust problems. Choose the defense that interrupts the specific attack rather than the most security-sounding phrase.

questions.question: Which command correctly verify whether port security has been configured on port FastEthernet 0/12 on a switch?

questions.question: Which is characteristic of satellite internet connection?
options: Their upload speed is about 10 percent of their download speed.

They use radio waves to communicate with cellular phone towers.

questions.question: Which type of wireless network uses transmitters to cover a medium-sized network, usually up to 300 feet (91.4 meters)?

questions.question: Which one command can be used to enable BPDU guard on a switch?

questions.question: The active and standby HSRP routers send hello packets to the HSRP group multicast address every 3 seconds by default.

questions.question: Which is characteristic of satellite internet connection?
options: They are frequently used by rural users without access to other high-speed connections.
They use radio waves to communicate with cellular phone towers.
They require a WiMax tower within 30 miles of the user location.
They are usually faster than cable and DSL connections.

questions.question: You can configure your WLAN Router through web browser.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. PC1 and PC2 should be able to obtain IP address assignments from the DHCP server. How many ports among switches should be assigned as trusted ports as part of the DHCP snooping configuration?

💡 Trusted = server replies allowed; untrusted = clients. Trust depends on traffic direction.

1) Start with the question: Decide whether the device is a client, server or relay. A new IPv4 client initially lacks a usable address and may not know a DHCP server. The server leases an address with configuration such as the mask, gateway and DNS servers.
2) Work through it: Follow DORA: Discover locates servers, Offer proposes a lease, Request identifies the chosen offer, and Acknowledgment confirms it. Initial discovery and selection use broadcast behavior; a renewal toward a known server can use unicast.
3) Apply the distinction: Check the layer named in the question. The IPv4 limited broadcast is 255.255.255.255; the Ethernet broadcast is FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-FF. DHCP uses UDP server port 67 and client port 68. A relay forwards client requests between subnets because routers do not normally forward local broadcasts.
❌ Common mix-ups: Do not confuse an offer with final confirmation, or renewal with rebinding/expiration. A 169.254.x.x self-assigned address usually indicates that no usable DHCP lease was obtained. questions.question: A network administrator is configuring a RADIUS server connection on a Cisco 3500 series WLC. The configuration requires a shared secret password. What is the purpose for the shared secret password?

1) Start with the question: Identify the wireless standard, frequency band and capability asked for before comparing choices. A rate, a frequency and an antenna feature describe different properties, so two statements can both be true while only one is offered in a particular variant.
2) Work through it: Use the core comparison: 802.11b operates at 2.4 GHz up to 11 Mb/s; 802.11g at 2.4 GHz up to 54 Mb/s; 802.11a at 5 GHz up to 54 Mb/s. 802.11n supports 2.4/5 GHz and MIMO, with a maximum theoretical 600 Mb/s; 802.11ac uses 5 GHz.
3) Apply the distinction: Check compatibility before moving clients between bands. A b/g-only client cannot use a 5 GHz radio just because the router is dual-band. Multiple antennas/spatial streams can improve capacity, while interference, shared airtime and protocol overhead reduce real application throughput.
❌ Common mix-ups: Advertised PHY rate is not guaranteed download speed. More channels or less congestion can help a suitable 5 GHz deployment, but it does not make every client compatible. IEEE 802.11 defines the WLAN family; IEEE 802.1Q instead concerns VLAN bridging/tagging.

questions.question: In wireless ad-hoc network _________
questions.explanation:
✅ In infrastructure mode a client communicates through an AP. In ad-hoc mode stations communicate directly without an AP. A capable NIC can support either mode depending on its driver and configuration.
💡 Ad hoc = peers directly; infrastructure = AP.

1) Start with the question: Classify the network by its intended geographic scope, rather than by the presence of radio alone. Personal, local, metropolitan and wide-area networks can all be wireless, but they support different kinds of coverage.
2) Work through it: A WPAN connects nearby personal devices, often using Bluetooth or ZigBee. A WLAN connects devices around a home, office or campus local network. A WMAN spans a metropolitan region, while a WWAN extends across much larger service areas.
3) Apply the distinction: Separate scope from topology. An infrastructure WLAN uses access points; an ad-hoc network connects peers directly. A BSS is one basic service set; connecting suitable service sets through a distribution system creates an ESS for broader local coverage.
❌ Common mix-ups: A distance quoted in a quiz is an example, not a universal boundary guaranteed by a standard. Likewise, having many APs does not automatically make a WLAN a wide-area network. Match the use case and the stated area.
